mainTopicBrief: 本单元围绕学习展开，涵盖找到自己的学习节奏（Reading）、毕业·落幕与启程（Extended reading）、规划未来与终身学习（Grammar and usage）和认识你的学习风格（Integrated skills）四个板块——学习方法与终身成长是高考应用文'演讲/书信'类的常见立意，也是雅思教育类议论文的经典命题，为选修系列收官。

subTopics.title: 找到自己的学习节奏
subTopics.desc: 课文核心：老师 impressed on us 一个道理——真正的学习并非千篇一律，你 are bound to change and grow，关键是找到 at one's own pace 的节奏，并 resolve to keep going。

prompts.task: 你的朋友 Lucy 因为学习进度比别人慢而焦虑。请你用英文回信开导她，内容包括：1. 表达理解；2. 谈谈学习节奏；3. 鼓励。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Dear Lucy,

I understand how anxious you feel when classmates seem to race ahead while you are still catching up. But please don't measure your journey by someone else's speed.

My teacher once impressed on me a simple truth: everyone learns at their own pace, and slower does not mean worse. What matters is that you keep moving and keep understanding, not that you finish first. You are bound to grow — I have already seen how much steadier your writing has become. So resolve to take one small step each day, and give yourself time.

Learning is a long road, not a short race. Trust your own pace, and you will arrive. I believe in you!

Yours,
Li Hua
vocabHints: measure your journey by someone else's speed
impressed on me a simple truth
resolve to take one small step

prompts.task: In many schools, all students of the same age study the same subjects at the same pace. Some people think students should instead be allowed to learn at their own pace. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
In most schools, children of the same age move through the same lessons together at a single, fixed pace. Some defend this shared rhythm; others argue that pupils should be free to progress at their own speed. Having weighed both, I believe a flexible pace suits learning better, provided schools can manage it fairly.

The traditional system has real strengths. Teaching a whole class together is efficient and affordable, allowing one teacher to reach many students; it builds a shared experience and friendships among peers; and a common standard makes it simple to measure progress and ensure everyone covers essential material. For schools with limited resources, uniform pacing is often the only practical option.

However, a single pace fits no one perfectly. Faster learners grow bored and waste potential waiting for others, while slower learners fall behind, lose confidence and may give up entirely, convinced they are simply "bad at" a subject. Allowing students to advance as they master each stage — quickly where they are strong, patiently where they struggle — respects the plain fact that people learn differently. Modern technology, moreover, increasingly makes such personalised learning practical even in large classes.

My own view is that flexible pacing is the better ideal, though it must be handled with care so that slower students receive support rather than neglect, and faster ones are stretched rather than simply pushed ahead alone.

In conclusion, while teaching everyone together is efficient and socially valuable, allowing students to learn at their own pace responds far better to how people actually learn. The wisest schools will combine shared classes with room for individual progress.

subTopics.title: 规划未来与终身学习
subTopics.desc: 语法板块核心词块：good prospects、be qualified for、regardless of occupation、keep learning——在飞速变化的世界，学历只是起点，持续学习才决定你能走多远。

prompts.task: 你校将举办 "My Future" 主题演讲。请你写一篇英文发言稿，谈谈你如何看待规划未来与持续学习，内容包括：1. 你的观点；2. 简要理由；3. 号召。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Good morning, everyone. When we talk about the future, many of us picture a single dream job with good prospects. But I'd like to suggest a different idea.

The world is changing so fast that the skills which qualify us for a job today may be out of date tomorrow. That is why, regardless of the occupation we end up in, the most important ability is not a fixed set of knowledge, but the habit of learning itself. A diploma may open a door, but only lifelong learning keeps us moving forward.

So let us plan boldly, yet stay humble enough to keep learning. The future belongs not to those who know the most today, but to those who never stop growing. Thank you!
vocabHints: a single dream job with good prospects
a diploma may open a door

prompts.task: In a fast-changing world, some people believe that the ability to keep learning throughout life is more important than the knowledge gained at school. To what extent do you agree or disagree? (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
As technology transforms work at unprecedented speed, some argue that the capacity to go on learning matters more than anything memorised at school. I largely agree, because in a world where knowledge dates quickly, the ability to keep learning is what protects and advances a person over a lifetime — though it depends on the foundation that school provides.

The strongest reason is the pace of change. Many students today will one day do jobs that do not yet exist and use technologies not yet invented. Facts learned at school, however useful now, may be obsolete within a decade, whereas the habit and skill of learning never expire. Workers who can retrain adapt to new industries and thrive, while those who rely only on old qualifications risk being left behind. Lifelong learning, in short, is the true form of job security in an uncertain age.

However, this does not make school knowledge worthless. On the contrary, the ability to keep learning is itself built at school — through literacy, reasoning, and a broad base of understanding on which all later learning depends. A person with no foundation cannot easily teach themselves; the two are not rivals but stages. School lays the groundwork, and lifelong learning builds upon it.

My view, therefore, is that while a solid education remains essential, its greatest gift is not a fixed store of facts but the equipment and appetite to keep learning.

In conclusion, in a fast-changing world the ability to keep learning is indeed more important than any fixed body of knowledge — yet it grows best from the strong foundation that good schooling provides.

subTopics.title: 认识你的学习风格
subTopics.desc: 综合技能板块核心：Auditory learners learn best when information is presented in a verbal manner，视觉型学习者则更依赖图像——认识自己的学习风格，就像画静物时懂得留白，找到最适合自己的方式。

prompts.task: 你校英文报开设 "Learn Smarter" 专栏。请你写一篇短文，介绍认识自己学习风格的重要性，内容包括：1. 什么是学习风格；2. 你的建议。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Have you ever wondered why a method that works for your friend does nothing for you? The answer may lie in learning styles.

People take in information differently. Visual learners remember best through pictures, charts and colours, while auditory learners learn best when information is presented in a verbal manner, such as when the teacher talks or they read aloud. Others learn most by doing. None is better than the rest — they are simply different doors into the same room.

So my advice is: get to know yourself. Notice when you learn most easily, then play to that strength — draw a mind map, record a note, or teach a classmate. Study is not about working harder alone; it is about working in the way that fits you best.
vocabHints: why a method that works for your friend
the answer may lie in learning styles
visual learners remember best through pictures
the way that fits you best

prompts.task: Some people believe that teachers should adapt their teaching to suit the different learning styles of individual students, while others think students should learn to adapt to the teacher's methods. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
Students clearly differ in how they learn best, and this raises a practical question: should teachers adjust their methods to each learner, or should learners adapt to the teacher? Both expectations contain wisdom, and in my opinion the responsibility runs both ways, though teachers should lead.

Those who want teachers to adapt make a humane point. Pupils absorb information differently — some through images, some through words, some through hands-on activity — and a teacher who uses only one approach inevitably fails part of the class. Varying methods, mixing explanation with visuals, discussion and practice, reaches more students and helps struggling ones who might otherwise conclude they are simply incapable. Good teaching, on this view, meets learners where they are.

Yet expecting teachers to tailor every lesson to thirty individuals is unrealistic, and it can leave students helpless. In real life — at university, at work — no one adjusts to our personal preferences; we must learn from lectures, manuals and methods not designed around us. A student who can only learn one way is fragile, whereas one who has learned to adapt to different teachers and formats gains a flexibility that serves them for life.

My own view is that both must move toward each other. Teachers should vary their methods enough to include the main learning styles and never rely on a single approach, while students should stretch themselves to cope with a range of teaching rather than demanding to be taught only their favourite way.

In conclusion, effective learning is a partnership: teachers should adapt as far as is practical, and students should learn to adapt too.

subTopics.title: 毕业·落幕与启程
subTopics.titleEn: Graduation: A Curtain and a Door
subTopics.desc: 拓展阅读核心：毕业典礼 brought down the curtain on my school life——但落幕也是启程，你将带着更成熟的自己，去 carve out a career，去找到 where you fit in。

prompts.task: 临近高中毕业，请你以 "Goodbye and Hello" 为题写一篇英文短文投稿校刊，记录你毕业时的心情，内容包括：1. 回望三年；2. 展望未来。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
The graduation ceremony brought down the curtain on my three years of high school, and my thoughts flashed back to the nervous student I once was.

So much has changed. I have grown more mature, learned where I fit in, and discovered what brings out the best in me. Saying goodbye to this campus and these friends is not easy; my throat felt tight as the final bell rang.

Yet every ending is also a beginning. Ahead of us lie new schools, new cities and one day careers we will carve out for ourselves. I am a little afraid, but mostly excited. Goodbye, my golden years — and hello, whatever comes next. I am ready.
vocabHints: brings out the best in me
every ending is also a beginning

prompts.task: Some people say that the years spent at school and university are the best years of a person's life. To what extent do you agree or disagree? (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
It is often said that school and university days are the happiest of our lives. I only partly agree: these years hold genuine and irreplaceable joys, but calling them the 'best' overlooks both their hidden pressures and the richer satisfactions that adult life can bring.

There is clearly truth in the claim. Student years combine relative freedom with few heavy responsibilities: young people are supported by their families, surrounded by friends their own age, and free to explore ideas and interests with time that adults rarely have again. Lifelong friendships are formed, first experiences are treasured, and the campus offers a protected space in which to grow and make mistakes cheaply. For many, these memories glow warmly for the rest of their lives.

Yet the picture is not wholly rosy. Student life also carries real stress — the fear of failure, examinations, uncertainty about the future and the ordinary pains of growing up — which nostalgia conveniently erases. Moreover, adult life brings its own deep rewards that school cannot: meaningful work, romantic love, raising a family, independence and the confidence that comes from mastering life. Many people are far happier and more settled at forty than they ever were at eighteen.

In my view, therefore, the school years are special but not automatically the best. They are one precious chapter, not the whole story, and to insist they are the peak is to undervalue everything that follows.

In conclusion, while student days offer joys worth cherishing, whether they are truly the best years depends on the person — and for many, the finest years still lie ahead.
